user.title: Data sources
user.description: Sensors for the battery and prices. The energy statistics are prefilled from the Energy Dashboard. Remove duplicates, for example two grid sources that measure the same meter. House load is computed as import − export + solar + battery discharge − battery charge.

data.price_entity: Electricity price sensor (with today/tomorrow price attributes)
data.wholesale_source: Wholesale price history (for prices not yet published)

data_description.soc_entity: A sensor with the battery's state of charge in % (0–100).
data_description.price_entity: A sensor whose attributes list today's (and tomorrow's) prices with their start times, such as the Nord Pool, EnergyZero, EPEX Spot, Tibber or Zonneplan integrations provide.
data_description.grid_import: Total energy taken from the grid (kWh, a meter reading that only goes up).
data_description.grid_export: Total energy fed into the grid (kWh).

data.wear_cost: Battery wear cost per kWh throughput

data_description.capacity_kwh: The usable capacity, not the nominal one: what the battery delivers from full to empty.
data_description.charge_eff: One-way efficiency from the grid into the battery (0.95 = 95%). Round trip is charge × discharge efficiency.
data_description.discharge_eff: One-way efficiency from the battery to the house or grid.
data_description.min_soc: The lowest state of charge the battery may reach. Must be below the maximum.
data_description.wear_cost: Cost of battery wear per kWh that goes through the battery. Vulpes only cycles the battery when the price difference beats this. Battery price ÷ (usable capacity × expected full cycles); 0.02–0.05 is typical.
data_description.max_import_w: From the main fuse, for example 3 × 25 A × 230 V = 17250 W.
data_description.max_export_w: The maximum power you may feed into the grid; often the same as the import limit.

tariff.title: Tariff
tariff.description: Prices for hours not yet published are estimated as a × wholesale + b. Export is paid as export a × wholesale + export b.

data.tariff_b: Import b (energy tax + markup, incl. VAT)

data_description.export_a: Usually 1: feed-in is paid at the market price without VAT. While net metering still applies to you, use the same values as Import a and b. Check your contract.
data_description.export_b: A feed-in fee per kWh as a negative number, a bonus as a positive one.

modes.title: Battery modes
modes.description: Tick the modes your system can do; Vulpes plans only with these. With grid setpoint (Victron ESS-style), charging holds grid import at the charge power and discharging holds grid export at the discharge power; with battery power, the battery itself runs at that power. Optionally pick the entity your current automation uses (for example an input_select) to compare the plan with what the house does. To let Vulpes control the battery, pick a control script: once the Active switch is on, Vulpes runs it every 15 minutes with what to do (see the field description).

data.power_control: How charge and discharge power is set
data.hold: Hold (charge from solar surplus only, never discharge)
data.self_consume: Self-consume (battery keeps the grid at zero)
data.pv_curtail: Solar can be switched off (for negative prices)
data.export_block: Export can be blocked (zero export, for negative prices)
data.mode_entity: Compare with an existing mode entity (optional)
data.control_script: Control script (optional, lets Vulpes control the battery)

data_description.idle: The battery neither charges nor discharges. The house runs on solar and the grid, and all solar surplus goes to the grid. Unlike Hold, it doesn't store solar surplus. Useful when exporting pays more than storing, for example to keep room in the battery for cheap or negative-price hours later in the day. Only enable it if your system has a standby or idle mode you can switch to.
data_description.export_block: Your inverter can stop feeding solar into the grid while still powering the house and charging the battery. Vulpes then also plans Hold, Self-consume and Idle with export blocked, and uses them when exporting would cost money.
data_description.control_script: Vulpes runs this script every 15 minutes while its Active switch is on, with the variables mode (charge, hold, self_consume, idle or discharge), pv_off, no_export, power_control, power_w, soc_min, soc_max, planned_grid_w, planned_battery_w, fallback and until. Without a usable plan, it sends self_consume with fallback set. Disable your own battery automations before you turn Active on.

compare.title: Compare with {entity}
compare.description: For each Vulpes mode, choose the state of {entity} that means the same. Leave empty if there is none; that state then counts as disagreeing with the plan.

data.hold: Hold (charge from solar only, no discharge)

solar.title: Solar arrays
solar.description: Describe your solar panels. Rough values are fine: calibration refines them from your history.{calibration}

menu_options.solar_json: Paste plane JSON (advanced: microinverters, several inverters)

solar_system.title: Solar inverter
solar_system.description: Group your panels into arrays: panels with the same direction and tilt. All arrays share one inverter. After setup, Vulpes compares these values with your solar history and proposes corrections: it does so once by itself, and any time you press **Calibrate solar** on the Vulpes EMS device. Map each array's string power sensor for the best result. Apply the result under Configure → Solar arrays.

data_description.array_count: Usually one per roof side, or one per inverter input (MPPT).
data_description.inverter_ac_w: The maximum AC output on the inverter's data sheet. For a hybrid inverter with a battery on the DC side, use the maximum PV input power instead: solar can then exceed the AC output while it charges the battery.

solar_array.title: Solar array {index} of {count}
solar_array.description: Rough values are fine; calibration corrects them later.

data_description.direction: Pick a compass direction or type degrees clockwise from north (180 = south).
data_description.kwp: Number of panels × watt-peak per panel, in kWp.
data_description.power_entity: The inverter's DC power sensor for the input (MPPT) this array is connected to. With it, calibration can fit this array's direction and tilt; without it, only the total size is corrected.

solar_json.title: Solar planes (JSON)
solar_json.description: Paste a JSON list of planes (azimuth, tilt, pdc0 in W, ac_max in W, optionally inverter), or the output of `vulpes-cli calibrate-solar`.

error.invalid_planes: Invalid planes JSON: each plane needs azimuth, tilt, pdc0 and ac_max.
error.invalid_direction: Pick a direction, or enter degrees between 0 and 360.
error.soc_unavailable: This sensor doesn't report a state of charge between 0 and 100 right now.
error.no_prices: This sensor has no price list in its attributes (a list of items with a start time and a price).
error.grid_import_required: Select at least one grid import statistic.
error.duplicate_statistic: Selected more than once: {statistic}. Each statistic may appear in only one field.
error.no_statistics: No hourly statistics in the last 60 days for: {statistic}. It needs a state_class and some history.
error.no_complete_hours: There is no hour in the last 60 days in which all selected statistics have data, so the house load can't be computed.
error.soc_range: The minimum state of charge must be below the maximum.
error.export_needs_import_a: With Import a at 0 the price does not follow the market, so the export price cannot either. Set Export a to 0 and put the fixed export price in Export b.
error.charge_w_too_high: The charge power is above the maximum charge power (battery power) or the maximum grid import (grid setpoint).
error.discharge_w_too_high: The discharge power is above the maximum discharge power (battery power) or the maximum grid export (grid setpoint).
error.no_mode_options: This entity has no options to compare with.

abort.no_mode_options: The selected mode entity lost its options during setup.

init.title: Vulpes EMS settings
init.description: Pick what to change. Each section is saved on its own.
